meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me on what basis you gave it, and whether anyone asked Owen about it first.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.

"The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." A misquoted line proves a seventeen-year-old got a quotation wrong, Hale, not who wrote the essay. Did you ask Owen where he got it before you entered the zero?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

"It seems to run in the family." You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale, because Claire won her appeal. I'm writing that down word for word, and the principal will be reading it before I leave this building.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect Owen's zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed and the principal next.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero", a plain admission of the process error that earned a flat "Okay."
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family", which brought in Claire and attacked Owen's character instead of his work.
Try next time: after raising the misquoted line, don't mention Claire; put a dated document of Owen's own work in front of her that she can check herself.
